reproResult: Followed the "Minimal reproduction" on my own worktree/instance at 16ceb3a54 (server :22525, daemon :30525, data dir under ~/.bb-dev/...wf_6b6686dc-4c2-10-fd7fce45b154). Steps 1-3 worked verbatim (parent thr_juvm8nstzq, children thr_6nkbcspvmj bad-model -> error, thr_jpjbsfdt9j -> idle). Step 4 (spawn-batch-children.sh) did NOT produce the batched "Child thread updates:" wording in my run: the two sequential spawns failed >2 s apart, so the parent got two separate single-child "[bb system] @thread:X failed." messages, and `bb thread search "Child thread updates"` legitimately returned active total 0 (phrase never existed). Spawning the two bad-model children in parallel (verify/spawn-parallel-children.sh) did yield the batched message (seq 310) and search then found it: active total 1, user_message seq 310 -- matching the report's core claim that [bb system] messages ARE indexed/searchable. Log checks reproduced exactly: --json default returned 100 events seq 1-230 (oldest, ascending) of a 177-event/max-seq-417 thread and did not contain the batched notification; human `--limit 500` errors "--limit and --after-seq are only supported with --format json"; minimal log grep -c 'bb system' = 2 vs verbose = 5 (mid-turn steer notifications collapsed). Both vitest files behave as stated (server test: 1 pass + intended failure on /older|omitted|truncat/; db test: 2 pass). Artifacts saved under /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1768/verify/. Not already fixed on origin/main (only 511d7db64 touches events.ts, unrelated; 0.38.0 tag has identical FTS indexing). Repro scripts hardcode the author's worktree path and a thread id, so I had to sed them before running.

findings.section: Root cause / 1. Search does index the notifications
findings.problem: The permalink and inline excerpt for the FTS-indexing claim point to the wrong code: packages/db/src/data/events.ts#L553-L585 at 16ceb3a54 is appendDaemonEventsInTransaction (high-water-mark bookkeeping), which does not upsert search segments. The prose says this excerpt 'upserts FTS segments for client/turn/requested' but the shown code does nothing of the kind, so the evidence visibly contradicts the claim.
findings.evidence: At 16ceb3a54: `sed -n 553,585p packages/db/src/data/events.ts` shows `export function appendDaemonEventsInTransaction(...)`. The real mechanism is listThreadSearchSegmentsForStoredEventArgs (L467-L497, `case "client/turn/requested": ... sourceKind: "user_message", text: extractVisiblePromptText(...)`) called from appendStoredThreadEventsInTransaction (L668-L724, `upsertThreadSearchSegments(db, {...})` at L718). The 553-585 numbers match the branch HEAD a108fa7ef, not the base commit the permalink names.
findings.fix: Re-point the permalink/excerpt to events.ts#L467-L497 and #L668-L724 (or #L718-L723) at 16ceb3a54 and re-extract the excerpt so it shows upsertThreadSearchSegments / the client/turn/requested -> user_message case.

findings.problem: The batched 'Child thread updates:' wording depends on both children failing inside a 2 s window, but the script spawns them sequentially (each `bb thread spawn` takes several seconds), so batching is a race the report presents as deterministic. In my run it did not batch, and `bb thread search "Child thread updates"` returned active total 0 — a reader following the steps literally could conclude the issue's search claim is TRUE, the opposite of the report's verdict.
findings.evidence: verify/08-spawn-batch-children.txt + verify/09-search-variants.txt: children thr_3cyteiurd6/thr_8piuy6nkcj produced separate single-child messages at seq 154 and 158; search 'Child thread updates' -> active total 0. Only after spawning two children in parallel (verify/spawn-parallel-children.sh) did seq 310 contain the batched text and search return total 1 (verify/09b-search-variants-after-parallel.txt). CHILD_THREAD_TURN_NOTIFICATION_BATCH_DELAY_MS = 2_000 in child-thread-notifications.ts:77.
findings.fix: Spawn the two bad-model children in parallel (background the two spawn commands and `wait`) or explicitly say the batching is timing-dependent and instruct the reader to verify with `bb thread log --json --limit 100000 | grep 'Child thread updates'` before running the search; make the search step's expected output conditional on that.

findings.problem: All three repro scripts (spawn-batch-children.sh, search-variants.sh, log-checks.sh) hardcode the author's worktree path /home/sawyer/projects/bb/.claude/worktrees/wf_242c3e11-a10-29/... as the CLI, and search-variants.sh hardcodes the author's child id thr_gdyx7rfjyx; log-checks.sh also writes 12-/13- JSON files into whatever directory it lives in. A clueless reader cannot copy-paste them.
findings.evidence: `CLI="node /home/sawyer/projects/bb/.claude/worktrees/wf_242c3e11-a10-29/packages/scripts/dist/commands/run-cli.js"` in all three scripts; `for q in ... "thr_gdyx7rfjyx" ...` in search-variants.sh. I had to sed both before running.
findings.fix: Use `${BB_CLI:-pnpm bb:dev}` or a relative `node packages/scripts/dist/commands/run-cli.js` from the repo root, take the child thread id from an env var, and write outputs to a caller-chosen directory.

findings.problem: The issue's strongest datapoint for the search claim — a parent 'whose own bb thread log shows it 23 times' yet search returned 0 — is not quoted or addressed as a claim row; the table only covers 'returns 0 hits even for a parent that received it'. A reader comparing issue to report will not see this reconciled (the hidden-thread and never-contained-the-phrase explanations are given, but neither obviously explains 23 visible occurrences).
findings.evidence: Issue body: 'Zero — including for the parent thread that had received the message minutes earlier, and whose own bb thread log shows it 23 times.' Report claims table has no row for this.
findings.fix: Add a row: Unverified/Refuted-with-caveat, stating that if the log truly showed the phrase 23 times, the only code path yielding 0 is a non-visible (hidden) parent thread (threads.ts:950), and note this remains unconfirmed without the reporter's thread visibility.

findings.section: Minimal reproduction / log windows and Environment
findings.problem: Unexplained numbers for a clueless reader: 'total events on thread: 177 max seq 373' (event count far below max seq) and 'events returned: 100 ... max seq 180' — the report never explains why sequence numbers are sparse (deleted/compacted delta events), which makes 'oldest 100' vs 'seq 1-180' look inconsistent. Also 'segment' is used before it is defined as 'a user-message row'.
findings.evidence: 14-log-checks.txt in the report; my run shows the same pattern (177 events, max seq 417). Definition of segment appears only later in Root cause section 2.
findings.fix: Add one sentence explaining that seq gaps are normal (some event rows are pruned/collapsed) and define 'segment' the first time it is used in TL;DR.

findings.problem: The report says minimal hides only the mid-turn (steer) notification and shows 2 of 3; in a longer session the gap is larger (my parent had 5 [bb system] messages, minimal showed 2, verbose 5). The claim is correct but understated; the report could note it scales with how many notifications arrive mid-turn.
findings.evidence: verify/14-log-checks.txt: minimal grep -c 'bb system' = 2, verbose = 5; seqs of [bb system] client/turn/requested: [19, 72, 154, 158, 310].
findings.fix: Phrase as 'every notification delivered while a turn is active is collapsed in minimal' rather than a one-off '2 of 3'.
